facts.statement: The genus Ankylosaurus was named by Barnum Brown in 1908.
facts.quote: It was named by Barnum Brown in 1908

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is possibly the largest known ankylosaurid, with an estimated length of 6 to 8 meters and a weight of 4.8 to 8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Possibly the largest known ankylosaurid, Ankylosaurus is estimated to have been between 6 and 8 m long and to have weighed between 4.8 and 8 MT

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus had a wide, low skull featuring two backward-pointing horns on the back of the head and two additional horns below them that pointed backward and downward.
facts.quote: It had a wide, low skull, with two horns pointing backward from the back of the head, and two horns below these that pointed backward and down

facts.statement: Unlike other ankylosaurs, Ankylosaurus nostrils faced sideways instead of forward.
facts.quote: Unlike other ankylosaurs, its nostrils faced sideways rather than towards the front

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was covered in osteoderms (armor plates) with bony half-rings on the neck and possessed a large club at the end of its tail.
facts.quote: It was covered in armor plates, or osteoderms, with bony half-rings covering the neck, and had a large club on the end of its tail

facts.statement: Bones in the skull and body of Ankylosaurus were fused to increase strength, a feature reflected in its genus name meaning 'fused lizard'.
facts.quote: Bones in the skull and other parts of the body were fused, increasing their strength, and this feature is the source of the genus name

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus likely fed as a non-selective browser, indicated by its broad muzzle.
facts.quote: Its broad muzzle indicates it was a non-selective browser

facts.statement: Researchers believe Ankylosaurus used its tail club for defense against predators or in fights with other Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: The tail club is thought to have been used in defense against predators or in intraspecific combat

facts.statement: The type specimen of Ankylosaurus magniventris was discovered in 1906 by Barnum Brown in the Hell Creek Formation near Gilbert Creek, Montana.
facts.quote: In 1906, an American Museum of Natural History expedition led by American paleontologist Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen of Ankylosaurus magniventris (AMNH 5895) in the Hell Creek Formation, near Gilbert Creek, Montana

facts.statement: Barnum Brown provided the scientific description of Ankylosaurus in 1908.
facts.quote: Brown scientifically described the animal in 1908

facts.statement: In 1910, Barnum Brown's expedition found an Ankylosaurus specimen in the Scollard Formation near the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: In 1910, another AMNH expedition led by Brown discovered an Ankylosaurus specimen (AMNH 5214) in the Scollard Formation by the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg and T. Potter Chamney collected a large Ankylosaurus skull in 1947 near the site of the 1910 discovery in Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1947 the American fossil collectors Charles M. Sternberg and T. Potter Chamney collected a skull and mandible (specimen CMN 8880, formerly NMC 8880), 1 km north of where the 1910 specimen was found

facts.statement: In 1990, Walter P. Coombs noted differences in the teeth of two Ankylosaurus skulls compared to the holotype, raising questions about their classification.
facts.quote: In 1990, American paleontologist Walter P. Coombs pointed out that the teeth of two skulls assigned to A. magniventris differed from those of the holotype specimen in some details

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus belongs to the family Ankylosauridae, with Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus as its closest relatives.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus is a member of the family Ankylosauridae, and its closest relatives appear to be Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was a quadrupedal dinosaur with a broad and robust body.
facts.quote: It was quadrupedal, with a broad, robust body

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was likely a slow-moving animal capable of making quick movements when needed.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus is thought to have been a slow-moving animal, able to make quick movements when necessary

facts.statement: Only a few Ankylosaurus specimens have been found, and no complete skeleton has been discovered yet.
facts.quote: A handful of specimens have been excavated to date, but a complete skeleton has not been discovered

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus jaws featured a beak at the front and rows of small, leaf-shaped teeth behind it.
facts.quote: The front part of the jaws was covered in a beak, with rows of small, leaf-shaped teeth farther behind it

facts.statement: The sinuses and nasal chambers in Ankylosaurus may have helped with heat and water balance or assisted in vocalization.
facts.quote: Sinuses and nasal chambers in the snout may have been for heat and water balance or may have played a role in vocalization

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus likely inhabited upland areas, as its ecological niche did not overlap with the nodosaurid Denversaurus.
facts.quote: Though it lived alongside Denversaurus, a nodosaurid ankylosaur, their ranges and ecological niches do not appear to have overlapped, and Ankylosaurus may have inhabited upland areas

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus coexisted with dinosaurs including Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops, and Edmontosaurus.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus also lived alongside dinosaurs such as Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops, and Edmontosaurus

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is considered the largest known ankylosaurine dinosaur and possibly the largest ankylosaurid.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus was the largest-known ankylosaurine dinosaur and possibly the largest ankylosaurid.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Roger B. J. Carpenter estimated the largest known Ankylosaurus skull (CMN 8880) belonged to an individual about 6.25 meters long with a hip height of 1.7 meters.
facts.quote: Carpenter estimated that the individual with the largest-known skull (specimen CMN 8880), which is 64.5 cm long and 74.5 cm wide, was about 6.25 m long and had a hip height of about 1.7 m.

facts.statement: In 2014, researchers Roger B. J. Benson and colleagues estimated the weight of the smallest known Ankylosaurus specimen (AMNH 5214) at 4.78 metric tons.
facts.quote: The English paleontologist Roger B. J. Benson and colleagues estimated the weight for AMNH 5214 at 4.78 MT in 2014.

facts.statement: In 2017, Arbour and Mallon estimated the length of the largest Ankylosaurus specimen (CMN 8880) to be between 7.56 and 9.99 meters.
facts.quote: In 2017, based on comparisons with more complete ankylosaurines, Arbour and Mallon estimated a length of 7.56 to 9.99 m for CMN 8880, and 6.02 to 7.95 m for AMNH 5214.

facts.statement: Arbour and Mallon tentatively estimated the weight of the largest Ankylosaurus specimen (CMN 8880) at 7.95 metric tons.
facts.quote: Arbour and Mallon estimated a weight of 4.78 MT for AMNH 5214, and tentatively estimated the weight of CMN 8880 at 7.95 MT.

facts.statement: The Ankylosaurus skull was low, triangular, and wider than it was long, with a broad and low back.
facts.quote: The skull was low and triangular in shape, and wider than it was long; the back of the skull was broad and low.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus possessed a broad beak located on the premaxillae bones of its skull.
facts.quote: The skull had a broad beak on the premaxillae.

facts.statement: Crests above the eye sockets merged into pyramidal-shaped upper squamosal horns that pointed backward and to the sides from the rear of the skull.
facts.quote: Crests above the orbits merged into the upper squamosal horns (their shape has been described as "pyramidal"), which pointed backwards to the sides from the back of the skull.

facts.statement: The snout region of Ankylosaurus underwent an extreme transformation compared to other ankylosaurs, making it unique among the group.
facts.quote: The snout region of Ankylosaurus was unique among ankylosaurs, and had undergone an "extreme" transformation compared to its relatives.

facts.statement: Unlike other ankylosaurids, the nostrils of Ankylosaurus were elliptical and directed downward and outward.
facts.quote: The nostrils were elliptical and were directed downward and outward, unlike in all other known ankylosaurids where they faced obliquely forward or upward.

facts.statement: Large, strap-like osteoderms on the sides of the snout completely covered the nostril openings, giving the snout a bulbous appearance.
facts.quote: Large loreal caputegulae—strap-like, side osteoderms of the snout—completely roofed the enlarged opening of the nostrils, giving a bulbous appearance.

facts.statement: The nasal cavities of Ankylosaurus were elongated and divided by a midline septum into two mirrored halves.
facts.quote: The nasal cavities (or chambers) of Ankylosaurus were elongated and separated by a septum at the midline, which divided the inside of the snout into two mirrored halves.

facts.statement: A ridge on the maxillae may have served as an attachment site for fleshy cheeks, though the existence of cheeks in ornithischians remains controversial.
facts.quote: The maxillae had a ridge that may have been the attachment site for fleshy cheeks; the presence of cheeks in ornithischians is controversial, but some nodosaurs had armor plates that covered the cheek region, which may have been embedded in the flesh.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus possessed small, leaf-shaped teeth that were compressed sideways.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus had small, phylliform (leaf-shaped) teeth, which were compressed sideways.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was a quadrupedal dinosaur with hind limbs longer than its forelimbs.
facts.quote: It was quadrupedal, and its hind limbs were longer than its forelimbs.

facts.statement: In the holotype specimen, the shoulder blade measured 61.5 cm in length and was fused with the coracoid bone.
facts.quote: In the holotype specimen, the scapula (shoulder blade) measures 61.5 cm long and was fused with the coracoid (a rectangular bone connected to the lower end of the scapula).

facts.statement: The upper arm bone of the AMNH 5214 specimen was short, very broad, and approximately 54 cm long.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) of AMNH 5214 was short, very broad and about 54 cm long.

facts.statement: The thigh bone of the AMNH 5214 specimen was 67 cm long and very robust.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone), also from AMNH 5214, was 67 cm long and very robust.

facts.statement: Although the feet are incompletely known, evidence suggests Ankylosaurus hindfeet likely had three toes, similar to advanced ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: While the feet of Ankylosaurus are incompletely known, the hindfeet probably had three toes, as is the case in advanced ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Ankylosaurus vertebrae contained ossified tendons that overlapped some of the vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neural spines had ossified (turned to bone) tendons, which also overlapped some of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus had distinctive armor made of bone knobs and plates called osteoderms embedded in its skin.
facts.quote: A prominent feature of Ankylosaurus was its armor, consisting of knobs and plates of bone known as osteoderms, or scutes, embedded in the skin.

facts.statement: The tail club of the specimen AMNH 5214 measured 60 cm in length, 49 cm in width, and 19 cm in height.
facts.quote: The tail club of AMNH 5214 is 60 cm long, 49 cm wide, and 19 cm tall.

facts.statement: The tail club of the largest known Ankylosaurus specimen may have been 57 cm wide.
facts.quote: The club of the largest specimen may have been 57 cm wide.

facts.statement: The handle of the Ankylosaurus tail club was formed by the last seven tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The last seven tail vertebrae formed the "handle" of the tail club.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn named the suborder Ankylosauria in 1923.
facts.quote: In 1923 Osborn coined the name Ankylosauria, thereby placing the ankylosaurids in their own suborder.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus belongs to the subfamily Ankylosaurinae within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus is considered part of the subfamily Ankylosaurinae (members of which are called ankylosaurines) within Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: The clade Thyreophora, which includes Ankylosaurus, existed from the Sinemurian age until the Maastrichtian, spanning 135 million years.
facts.quote: Ankylosauria and Stegosauria are now grouped together within the clade Thyreophora. This group first appeared in the Sinemurian age, and survived for 135 million years until disappearing in the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The Ankylosaurus tail club was semicircular from above, distinguishing it from the pointed clubs of Anodontosaurus and the narrow clubs of Dyoplosaurus.
facts.quote: The tail club of Ankylosaurus was semicircular when seen from above, similar to those of Euoplocephalus and Scolosaurus but unlike the pointed club osteoderms of Anodontosaurus or the narrow, elongated club of Dyoplosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Arbour and Currie disputed Carpenter's interpretation of Ankylosaurus cervical armor, noting the holotype fragments did not fit his proposed arrangement, though breakage might explain the discrepancy.
facts.quote: Arbour and the Canadian paleontologist Philip J. Currie disagreed with Carpenter's interpretation in 2015 and pointed out that the cervical half-ring fragments of the holotype specimen did not fit together in the way proposed by Carpenter (though this could be due to breakage).

facts.statement: Arbour and Mallon proposed that Ankylosaurus cervical armor consisted of continuous U-shaped yokes with six keeled osteoderms on each side.
facts.quote: Arbour and Mallon elaborated on this idea, describing the shape of these half-rings as "continuous U-shaped yokes" over the upper part of the neck, and suggested that Ankylosaurus had six keeled osteoderms with oval bases on each half-ring.

facts.statement: It remains unknown whether Ankylosaurus had osteoderms on its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: It is unknown whether the hindlimbs bore osteoderms.

facts.statement: The U-shaped zygapophyses and neural spines of Ankylosaurus tail vertebrae differ from the V-shape of most other ankylosaurids, possibly due to a wider tail handle.
facts.quote: The interlocked zygapophyses (articular processes) and neural spines of the handle vertebrae were U-shaped when seen from above, whereas those of most other ankylosaurids are V-shaped, which may be due to the handle of Ankylosaurus being wider.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was a herbivore, like other ornithischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other ornithischians, Ankylosaurus was herbivorous.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus had a wide muzzle adapted for non-selective low-browse cropping.
facts.quote: Its wide muzzle was adapted for non-selective low-browse cropping

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus likely fed on abundant ferns and low-growing shrubs.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus probably fed on abundant ferns and low-growing shrubs.

facts.statement: If endothermic, Ankylosaurus would have consumed approximately 60 kg of ferns per day.
facts.quote: Assuming it was endothermic, Ankylosaurus would have eaten 60 kg of ferns per day

facts.statement: Fossil teeth of Ankylosaurus show wear on the crown face rather than the tip, suggesting chewing behavior.
facts.quote: Fossils of Ankylosaurus teeth exhibit wear on the face of the crown rather than on the tip of the crown

facts.statement: In 1982, Carpenter identified two baby Ankylosaurus teeth measuring 3.2 to 3.3 mm from the Lance and Hell Creek Formations.
facts.quote: In 1982 Carpenter ascribed to baby Ankylosaurus two very small teeth that originate from the Lance and Hell Creek Formations and measure 3.2 to 3.3 mm in length, respectively.

facts.statement: Because adults did little chewing, Ankylosaurus likely spent less time foraging than an elephant.
facts.quote: Since adult Ankylosaurus did little chewing of its food, it would have spent less time in the day foraging than an elephant.

facts.statement: The broad ribcage suggests Ankylosaurus may have digested unchewed food via hindgut fermentation similar to modern herbivorous lizards.
facts.quote: Based on the broadness of the ribcage, the digestion of unchewed food may have been facilitated by hindgut fermentation like in modern herbivorous lizards

facts.statement: In 1969, Georg Haas concluded that ankylosaur skull musculature was relatively weak despite the large skull size.
facts.quote: In 1969, paleontologist Georg Haas concluded that despite the large size of ankylosaur skulls, the associated musculature was relatively weak.

facts.statement: In 2017, Arbour and Mallon compared the retracted nostrils of Ankylosaurus to those of digging worm lizards and blind snakes.
facts.quote: The retracted position of the nostrils of Ankylosaurus were compared to those of fossorial (digging) worm lizards and blind snakes by Arbour and Mallon in 2017

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Ankylosaurus may have been omnivorous based on low tooth formation rates and other factors.
facts.quote: These factors, as well as the low rate of tooth formation in ankylosaurs compared to other ornithischians, indicate that Ankylosaurus may have been omnivorous (eating both plant and animal matter).

facts.statement: Studies indicate nodosaurs had higher relative bite force than ankylosaurids, suggesting diverging jaw mechanics and dietary partitioning.
facts.quote: This indicates that while the two groups converged in some features, the nodosaurs had higher relative bite force, which suggests diverging jaw mechanics and dietary partitioning between the two.

facts.statement: In 1977, Teresa Maryańska proposed ankylosaur sinuses may have lightened the skull, housed a gland, or aided vocal resonance.
facts.quote: In 1977, paleontologist Teresa Maryańska proposed that the complex sinuses and nasal cavities of ankylosaurs may have lightened the weight of the skull, housed a nasal gland, or acted as a chamber for vocal resonance.

facts.statement: Carpenter rejected the idea that ankylosaur sinuses aided vocalization or significantly reduced skull weight.
facts.quote: Carpenter rejected these hypotheses, arguing that tetrapod animals make sounds through the larynx, not the nostrils, and that reduction in weight was minimal

facts.statement: A 2011 study suggested Euoplocephalus nasal passages functioned as a heat and water balancing system.
facts.quote: A 2011 study of the nasal passages of Euoplocephalus by paleontologist Tetsuto Miyashita and colleagues supported their function as a heat and water balancing system

facts.statement: Inner ear reconstructions suggest Ankylosaurus was adapted to hear low frequencies, possibly from nasal resonant sounds.
facts.quote: Reconstructions of the inner ear suggest adaptation to hearing at low frequencies, such as the low-toned resonant sounds possibly produced by the nasal passages.

facts.statement: The enlarged olfactory region indicates Ankylosaurus had a well-developed sense of smell.
facts.quote: The enlarged olfactory region of ankylosaurids indicates a well-developed sense of smell.

facts.statement: Carpenter argued the nasal chamber shape indicates unidirectional airflow looping through the lungs.
facts.quote: According to Carpenter, the shape of the nasal chambers of Ankylosaurus indicate that airflow was unidirectional (looping through the lungs during inhalation and exhalation)

facts.statement: The orbit position suggests Ankylosaurus had some stereoscopic vision.
facts.quote: The position of the orbits of Ankylosaurus suggest some stereoscopic vision.

facts.statement: Coombs suggested ankylosaurs may have been capable diggers, though limited by their hoof-like hands.
facts.quote: In addition, Coombs suggested that ankylosaurs may have been capable diggers, though the hoof-like structure of the manus would have limited fossorial activity.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurs were likely slow-moving but capable of quick movements when necessary.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurs were likely to have been slow-moving and sluggish animals, though they may have been capable of quick movements when necessary.

facts.statement: The blunter squamosal horns in larger Ankylosaurus specimens compared to smaller ones may represent ontogenetic variation.
facts.quote: The squamosal horns of the largest Ankylosaurus specimen are blunter than those of the smallest specimen, which is also the case in Euoplocephalus, and this may represent ontogenetic variation (related to growth development).

facts.statement: Studies show juvenile ankylosaur ribs fused with vertebrae during development.
facts.quote: Studies of specimens of Pinacosaurus of different ages found that during ontogenetic development, the ribs of juvenile ankylosaurs fused with their vertebrae.

facts.statement: Forelimbs became more robust while hindlimbs did not grow relatively larger, supporting the idea that arms bore most of the weight.
facts.quote: The forelimbs strongly increased in robustness while the hindlimbs did not become larger relative to the rest of the skeleton, further evidence that the arms bore most of the weight.

facts.statement: Skull bone plates in Ankylosaurus first ossified at the snout and rear rim before extending to the middle.
facts.quote: On the skull, the middle bone plates first ossified at the snout and the rear rim, with ossification gradually extending towards the middle regions.

facts.statement: Body ossification in Ankylosaurus progressed from the neck backward toward the tail.
facts.quote: On the rest of the body, ossification progressed from the neck backward in the direction of the tail.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus had thin osteoderms reinforced by randomly distributed cushions of collagen fibers embedded directly into the bone tissue.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of ankylosaurids were thin in comparison to those of other ankylosaurs, and appear to have been strengthened by randomly distributed cushions of collagen fibers.

facts.statement: The collagen-reinforced armor of Ankylosaurus was lightweight, durable, and resistant to predator teeth.
facts.quote: This would have provided the ankylosaurids with an armor covering that was both lightweight and highly durable, being resistant to breakage and penetration by the teeth of predators.

facts.statement: Palpebral bones over the eyes of Ankylosaurus may have provided additional eye protection.
facts.quote: The palpebral bones over the eyes may have provided additional protection for them.

facts.statement: The tail club of Ankylosaurus was an active defensive weapon capable of breaking the bones of an attacker.
facts.quote: The tail club of Ankylosaurus seems to have been an active defensive weapon, capable of producing enough of an impact to break the bones of an assailant.

facts.statement: Partially ossified and inelastic tail tendons in Ankylosaurus allowed great force to be transmitted to the tail club.
facts.quote: The tendons of the tail were partially ossified and were not very elastic, allowing great force to be transmitted to the club when it was used as a weapon.

facts.statement: Researchers could not determine whether Ankylosaurus used its tail club for defense against predators, intraspecific combat, or both.
facts.quote: Despite the feasibility of tail-swinging, the researchers could not determine whether ankylosaurids used their clubs for defense against potential predators, in intraspecific combat, or both.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus lived between 68 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus existed between 68 and 66 million years ago, in the final, or Maastrichtian, stage of the Late Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was among the last dinosaur genera to appear before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: It was among the last dinosaur genera that appeared before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Ankylosaurus comes from the Hell Creek Formation in Montana, with other fossils found in Wyoming, Alberta, and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: The type specimen is from the Hell Creek Formation of Montana, while other specimens have been found in the Lance and Ferris Formations in Wyoming, the Scollard Formation in Alberta, and the Frenchman Formation in Saskatchewan, all of which date to the end of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The rarity of Ankylosaurus fossils suggests it was ecologically rare or restricted to uplands where fossilization was less likely.
facts.quote: Fossils of Ankylosaurus are rare in the sediments it is known from, and the distribution of its remains suggests that it was ecologically rare, or restricted to the uplands of the formations, where it would have been less likely to fossilize, rather than the coastal lowlands.

facts.statement: Due to its low center of gravity, Ankylosaurus could not knock down trees like modern elephants.
facts.quote: With its low center of gravity, Ankylosaurus would have been unable to knock down trees like modern elephants do.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was incapable of chewing bark and unlikely to have practiced bark stripping.
facts.quote: It was also incapable of chewing bark and thus unlikely to have practiced bark stripping.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus lived in a warm subtropical/temperate monsoonal climate with occasional rainfall, tropical storms, and forest fires.
facts.quote: The regions where Ankylosaurus and other Late Cretaceous ankylosaurs have been found had a warm subtropical/temperate climate, which was monsoonal, had occasional rainfall, tropical storms, and forest fires.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus shared its environment with Triceratops, Torosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Edmontosaurus, Pachycephalosaurus, and theropods like Struthiomimus, Ornithomimus, Pectinodon, and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus shared its environment with other dinosaurs that included the ceratopsids Triceratops and Torosaurus, the hypsilophodont Thescelosaurus, the hadrosaurid Edmontosaurus, an indeterminate nodosaur, the pachycephalosaurian Pachycephalosaurus, and the theropods Struthiomimus, Ornithomimus, Pectinodon, and Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus became the best-known ankylosaur in popular culture, possibly due to a life-sized reconstruction at the 1964 World's Fair in New York City.
facts.quote: Carpenter noted in 2004 that Ankylosaurus has become the archetypal member of its group, and the best-known ankylosaur in popular culture, perhaps due to a life-sized reconstruction of the animal being featured at the 1964 World's Fair in New York City.

facts.statement: Many traditional depictions show Ankylosaurus in a squatting posture with a huge tail club dragged over the ground.
facts.quote: Many traditional popular depictions show Ankylosaurus in a squatting posture and with a huge tail club being dragged over the ground.

facts.statement: Modern reconstructions depict Ankylosaurus with an upright limb posture and the tail held off the ground.
facts.quote: Modern reconstructions show the animal with a more upright limb posture and with the tail held off the ground.

facts.statement: Large sideways spines seen in traditional depictions are not known from Ankylosaurus itself.
facts.quote: Large spines projecting sideways from the body (similar to those of nodosaurid ankylosaurs) are present in many traditional depictions, but are not known from Ankylosaurus itself.

facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1908

facts.quote: species_authority: Brown, 1908

facts.statement: Anchylosaurus magniventris Sternberg, 1909 is a synonym of Ankylosaurus magniventris.
facts.quote: synonyms: Anchylosaurus magniventris Sternberg, 1909

facts.statement: The smallest known skull, specimen AMNH 5214, measures 55.5 cm in length and 64.5 cm in width.
facts.quote: El cráneo más pequeño conocido, el espécimen AMNH 5214 es de 55,5 cm de largo y 64,5 cm de ancho

facts.statement: This smaller specimen is estimated to have measured between 5.4 meters in length and around 1.4 meters in height.
facts.quote: y se estima que este espécimen que habría medido entre 5,4 m de largo y alrededor de 1,4 m de altura

facts.statement: Other authors have proposed lengths ranging from 7 meters to over 9 meters.
facts.quote: Otros autores han propuesto una longitud de 7 m, 8-9 m, o más de 9 m

facts.statement: The structure of most of the Ankylosaurus skeleton, including most of the pelvis, tail, and feet, is still unknown.
facts.quote: La estructura de la mayor parte del esqueleto de Ankylosaurus, incluyendo la mayor parte de la pelvis, la cola y los pies, aún se desconoce

facts.statement: The structure of its body was low and very wide.
facts.quote: La estructura de su cuerpo era baja y muy ancha

facts.statement: It was a quadruped with hind limbs longer than the front limbs.
facts.quote: Fue un dinosaurio cuadrúpedo, con los miembros traseros más largos que los delanteros

facts.statement: The humerus was short and very wide, measuring around 54 cm in length in specimen AMNH 5214.
facts.quote: El húmero era corto y muy ancho de alrededor de 54 cm de longitud en la espécimen del AMNH 5214

facts.statement: The femur was very robust and 67 cm long in specimen AMNH 5214.
facts.quote: El fémur era muy robusto, y 67 cm de largo en AMNH 5214

facts.statement: The hind feet probably had three toes, as is the case in related animals.
facts.quote: la patas traseras probablemente tenía tres dedos de los pies, como es el caso en los animales relacionados

facts.statement: Like other ankylosaurians, Ankylosaurus was herbivorous.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros anquilosaurianos, Ankylosaurus era herbívoro

facts.statement: Its mouth was equipped with small, leaf-shaped teeth suitable for cutting vegetation.
facts.quote: su boca estaba dotada de pequeños dientes con forma de hoja que eran aptos para cortar la vegetación

facts.statement: These teeth were the smallest in comparison to the body of any other ankylosaurid.
facts.quote: los más pequeños en comparación al cuerpo de cualquier otro anquilosáurido

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus did not share the grinding tooth series of contemporary ceratopsids and hadrosaurs, demonstrating very little chewing.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus no compartía las series de dientes moledores de los ceratópsidos y hadrosáuridos contemporáneos, demostrando una masticación muy escasa

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae had large neural spines that increased in height toward the body.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales tenía grandes espinas neurales que el aumentan en altura hacia el cuerpo

facts.statement: The front of the neural spines had entheses, common in well-developed adult dinosaurs, indicating the presence of large ligaments that helped support the massive head.
facts.quote: La parte delantera de las espinas neurales había entesis, que era común entre los dinosaurios adultos bien desarrollados, e indica la presencia de grandes ligamentos que ayudaron a apoyar la cabeza masiva

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae were closely spaced, limiting downward movement of the back.
facts.quote: Las vértebras dorsales estaban estrechamente espaciadas, lo que limita el movimiento hacia abajo de la espalda

facts.statement: Tendons had ossified on the neural spines, which also overlapped some of the vertebrae.
facts.quote: En las espinas neurales se habían osificado tendones, que también se superponen algunas de las vértebras

facts.statement: The ribs of the last four vertebrae were fused to them, and the ribcage was very wide in this part of the body.
facts.quote: Las costillas de las últimas cuatro vértebra estaban fusionadas a ellas, y la caja torácica fue muy amplia en esta parte del cuerpo

facts.statement: The caudal vertebrae had centers that were slightly amphicoelous, meaning concave on both sides.
facts.quote: La vértebra caudalestenía centros que fueron ligeramente amfhicoelos, lo que significa que se cóncavos en ambos lados

facts.statement: The skull of Ankylosaurus was low and triangular in shape, wider than it was long.
facts.quote: El cráneo fue bajo y de forma triangular, más ancho que largo.

facts.statement: Fused crests above the eye sockets formed upper horns on the squamosal bone, described as pyramidal and pointing backward toward the sides of the skull.
facts.quote: Crestas por encima de las órbitas se fusionan para formar los cuernos superiores del escamoso su forma ha sido descrito como " piramidal ", que señaló apuntaban atrás a los lados de la parte posterior del cráneo.

facts.statement: Jugal horns were present on the skull, pointing backward and downward.
facts.quote: Los cuernos yugales estaban presentes, que apuntaba hacia atrás y hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Each side of the snout contained five sinuses, four of which expanded into the maxilla bone.
facts.quote: Cada lado del hocico tenía cinco senos, cuatro de los cuales se expandieron en el maxilar hueso.

facts.statement: The maxillae expanded to the sides, creating a bulge that may have been caused by internal sinuses.
facts.quote: Los maxilares se expandieron a los lados, dando la impresión de un bulto, que puede haber sido debido a los senos en su interior.

facts.statement: Specimen AMNH 5214 has 34 to 35 tooth sockets in the upper jaw, more than any other ankylosaurid.
facts.quote: El espécimen AMNH 5214 tiene 34-35 alvéolos dentales en el maxilar superior, más dientes que cualquier otro anquilosáurido.

facts.statement: The lower jaw was low relative to its length, and the tooth row was nearly straight rather than arched when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: La mandíbula de Ankylosaurus era baja en proporción a su longitud, y la fila de dientes estaba casi en línea recta en lugar de arqueada, cuando se ve desde el lado.

facts.statement: The incomplete lower jaw of the largest specimen, NMC 8880, is the same length as that of the smallest specimen.
facts.quote: La mandíbula incompleta de la muestra más grandes, NMC 8880 es de la misma longitud.

facts.statement: The teeth were mostly taller than they were wide and very small relative to the size of the skull.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran en su mayoría más alto de lo que anchos, y eran muy pequeños en relación con el tamaño del cráneo.

facts.statement: The tooth denticles were large, numbering between six and eight at the front of the tooth and five to seven at the back.
facts.quote: Los dentículos eran grandes, su número en el intervalo de seis a ocho en la parte frontal del diente, y cinco a siete atrás.

facts.statement: The most prominent feature of Ankylosaurus was its armor, consisting of buttons and bone plates known as osteoderms or shields embedded in the skin.
facts.quote: La característica más prominente de Ankylosaurus era su armadura, que consiste de los botones y las placas de hueso conocidas como osteodermos o escudos incrustados en la piel.

facts.statement: Osteoderms varied from 1 cm in diameter to 35.5 cm in length and also varied in shape.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos variaron de 1 cm de diámetro a 35,5 cm de longitud, y también variaron en forma.

facts.statement: The body-covering osteoderms were very flat, though with a low keel on one margin.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos que cubren el cuerpo eran muy plana, aunque con una quilla baja en un margen.

facts.statement: Like other ankylosaurids, Ankylosaurus had semi-cervical rings, armor plates on the neck, but these are only known from fragments, making their exact arrangement uncertain.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros anquilosáuridos, Ankylosaurus tenía medios anillos cervicales, placas de armadura en el cuello, pero éstos solo son conocidos a partir de fragmentos, haciendo su disposición exacta incierta.

facts.statement: The tail club of Ankylosaurus consists of two large osteoderms, with a row of small osteoderms along the midline and two small osteoderms at the tip.
facts.quote: La porra de la cola de Ankylosaurus se compone de dos grandes osteodermos, con una fila de pequeños osteodermos en la línea media, y dos pequeños osteodermos en la punta.

facts.statement: The tail club of specimen AMNH 5214 measures 450 mm in width.
facts.quote: La porra de la cola del AMNH 5214 mide 450 mm de ancho.

facts.statement: The last seven tail vertebrae form the "handle" of the tail club.
facts.quote: Las últimas siete vértebras de la cola forman el "mango" de la porra de la cola.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons attached to the vertebrae in front of the tail club, and these features together helped strengthen it.
facts.quote: Tendones osificados unidos a las vértebras en frente de la porra de la cola, y estas características juntas ayudaron a fortalecerlo.

facts.statement: A 2009 study showed that large tail clubs could generate enough force to break bones during impacts, but medium and small ones could not.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2009 mostró que las "grandes bolas de la cola podrían generar la fuerza suficiente para romper los huesos durante los impactos, pero las medianas y pequeñas no podrían"

facts.statement: It was proposed that the tail club might have served as a decoy for the head, but this hypothesis has been heavily discredited.
facts.quote: Se propuso también que pudo servir como un señuelo para la cabeza, sin embargo esta hipótesis ha sido muy desacreditada.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Victoria M. Arbour and Philip J. Currie disagreed with Carpenter's interpretation, noting that fragments of the semi-cervical rings from specimen AMNH 5895 do not fit together as Carpenter proposed, though this could be due to their condition.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos Victoria M. Arbour y Philip J. Currie no estaban de acuerdo con la interpretación del Carpenter, y señalaron que los fragmentos de la mitad de los anillos cervicales del espécimen AMNH 5895 no encajan entre sí de la manera propuesta por Carpenter, aunque esto podría ser debido a su estado.

facts.statement: Instead, they suggested that the fragments represent the remains of two semi-cervical rings that formed two semi-circular armor plates around the top of the neck, as in the closely related Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: En su lugar, sugirieron que los fragmentos representan los restos de dos medios anillos del cuello, que se formaron dos placas semicirculares de la armadura alrededor de la parte superior del cuello, como en los estrechamente relacionados Anodontosaurus y Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus belongs to the parent group Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is classified in the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
